# AWS HPC Recipes

> A comprehensive collection of infrastructure-as-code recipes for building High Performance Computing (HPC) systems on AWS. The recipes center on AWS Parallel Computing Service (PCS), the managed Slurm service, and also cover AWS ParallelCluster, Research and Engineering Studio (RES), and AWS Batch.

This repository contains 100+ tested recipes organized by HPC use case, from basic networking setups to advanced multi-user clusters with accounting. Each recipe includes CloudFormation templates, documentation, and quick-launch links for immediate deployment across all AWS regions including GovCloud and China partitions.

Key technologies covered: AWS PCS, ParallelCluster, Slurm, EFA networking, FSx storage systems, EFS, S3, Graviton processors, and specialized HPC instance types.

## Validation & CI

All recipes are validated on every push via GitLab CI. Run locally with:

```bash
make validate
```

This runs four checks in sequence:
1. `scripts/validate_structure.py` — every recipe has required files and directories
2. `scripts/validate_metadata.py` — `metadata.yml` conforms to schema and uses valid semver
3. `scripts/validate_partitions.py` — no hardcoded `arn:aws:` (must use `${AWS::Partition}`)
4. `cfn-lint` — CloudFormation template linting (errors only; warnings suppressed via `.cfnlintrc`)

Lines with `# partition-exception: <reason>` are excluded from partition checks for AWS-owned resources that are genuinely partition-specific.

## Core Services

- [AWS Parallel Computing Service (PCS) Recipes](recipes/pcs/): The managed Slurm service. Start here for new HPC clusters on AWS.
- [ParallelCluster Recipes](recipes/pcluster/): Recipes for self-managed Slurm clusters.
- [Research and Engineering Studio Recipes](recipes/res/): Desktop and visualization environments.
- [Networking Recipes](recipes/net/): HPC-optimized VPC configurations.
